originality.rationale: Primary SPAI research establishes Frobenius minimization and pattern selection but not the local sign formula/all-weight star characterization. Most relevant direct M-matrix treatment Wang–Lawlor–Kale Theorem 3.7 explicitly assumes computed inverse nonnegativity; our claim determines its failure and a sharp topology regime where it holds. Related published records address different algorithms and objectives. Remaining priority risk is unindexed older results.
residual_risks: Full text of Holland–Wathen–Shaw 2005/2006 was not accessible; publisher abstract alone cannot rule out equivalent statements in the body.
Old preprints, theses, or unindexed fixed-pattern sign studies may contain an equivalent tree result; novelty is supported by examined sources rather than certified publication priority.
The theorem is about one specific unconstrained right Frobenius problem; alternative symmetry-constrained or nonnegative-constrained minimizers are not compared.

value.rationale: A complete topology iff law and local test for sign preservation identify exactly when the condition needed for M-matrix preconditioner guarantees is robust to all conductances. Homogeneous trees remain strictly positive, while a minimal length-three path with heterogeneous weights can violate positivity despite strict diagonal dominance. This distinguishes a structural obstruction from isolated numerical counterexamples and informs order-preserving sparse inverse design.
